alternatives.title: Günter Last and Mathew Penrose, Lectures on the Poisson Process

per_item.argument: The source defines point processes as random counting measures and locally finite point processes on metric spaces. The tagged-particle limit and the Bernoulli mark law are constructed and proved locally.

The definition of locally finite counting measures and the vague topology is recorded with this independently inspected full-text treatment; the item explicitly avoids deriving expectation convergence from vague convergence.

alternatives.title: Olav Kallenberg, Foundations of Modern Probability, 1997
alternatives.locator: Chapter 4, Theorem 4.19 and Lemma 4.20, printed pp. 75–77.

per_item.argument: The source defines the vague topology on locally finite measures by compactly supported continuous test functions and distinguishes vague convergence from weak convergence when mass escapes to infinity. The item defines local-count uniform integrability as a condition without asserting an unproved convergence theorem.

sources.title: Sascha Friedli and Yvan Velenik, Statistical Mechanics of Lattice Systems: A Concrete Mathematical Introduction, complete revised author PDF
sources.locator: Chapter 3, Section 3.4, printed pp. 94–95; Chapter 6, Section 6.9, printed pp. 298–300; Appendix B.12, printed pp. 510–512.

contents.name: Finite-spin configurations, local observables, and local convergence

source_review.read_extent: Read all of Chapter 3, Section 3.4, including Definitions 3.11, 3.13, 3.14 and Remarks 3.12 and 3.15, at printed pp. 94–95.
source_review.supports: The finite-spin configuration space and the use of finite-coordinate observables to describe local convergence.
source_review.limitations: The item supplies its own explicit weighted cylinder metric and proves compactness and equivalence with weak convergence locally.

contents.name: Weak limits on the finite-spin configuration space

source_review.read_extent: Read the same complete local-observable passage in Chapter 3, Section 3.4, and the weak-limit setup it points to in Chapter 6.
source_review.supports: Comparison for convergence tested on local functions and the relation to weak limits of probability measures.
source_review.limitations: The equivalence for every finite alphabet is proved locally by a cylinder-function uniform approximation.

contents.name: Finite relative entropy, the Gibbs variational identity, and grouping

source_review.read_extent: Read Chapter 6, Section 6.9, Lemma 6.76 and its proof at printed pp. 298–300, and Appendix B.12, Definitions B.64–B.66 and Exercise B.23 with its cited use at printed pp. 510–512.
source_review.supports: Finite relative entropy conventions, nonnegativity, and the log-sum/Jensen mechanism behind grouping monotonicity.
source_review.limitations: The finite joint chain rule and each zero-mass boundary case are derived in the local proof; the source's exercise is not treated as a complete proof.

sources.title: James R. Norris, Advanced Probability, complete author-hosted lecture notes
sources.locator: Section 2.4, Theorems 2.4.1–2.4.2; Section 4.1 and Section 4.3, Theorems 4.3.1–4.3.2; Section 5.1, printed pp. 30–31.

contents.name: Product-space local convergence and ordinary weak convergence

source_review.read_extent: Read the full definition of weak convergence in Section 5.1 and the complete surrounding characterization discussion, printed pp. 30–31.
source_review.supports: The weak-convergence convention used by the local equivalence proof.
source_review.limitations: Norris does not prove the finite-spin cylinder equivalence; that proof is local.

contents.name: Càdlàg martingales and finite-horizon maximal estimates

source_review.read_extent: Read the càdlàg definition in Section 4.1, the dyadic-grid reduction and Theorem 4.3.2 in Section 4.3, printed pp. 25–27, and the discrete maximal-inequality proof in Section 2.4.
source_review.supports: The continuous-time path regularity and dyadic sampling method for Doob's bound.
source_review.limitations: The local proof uses the exact finite-terminal discrete inequality from the pinned mathematical supplier and proves the finite-horizon limit.

source_review.read_extent: Read the full continuous-time filtration and martingale definitions in Section 4.3 and its discrete-time sampling argument.
source_review.supports: The all-pairs martingale convention and continuous-time path-space context.
source_review.limitations: The source does not supply the finite-state generator bracket formula; the full semigroup and finite-jump derivation is local.

contents.name: Finite rate-matrix chains and all-pairs transition identities

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete Section 4.3 continuous-time Markov-chain treatment and the Section 4.1 path convention.
source_review.supports: The row-generator, transition-semigroup, and càdlàg path conventions used by the local definition.
source_review.limitations: The local definition supplies its exact exponential-clock convention; existence for reducible generators is proved locally.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete Section 4.3 continuous-time chain construction and transition discussion.
source_review.supports: A comparison treatment for finite-state continuous-time chains and their semigroups.
source_review.limitations: The local proof covers reducible chains, zero exit rates, independence of clocks, nonexplosion, and the conditional transition identity.

sources.title: Rick Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition, complete author-hosted PDF
sources.locator: Chapter 4, Section 4.4, Theorems 4.4.2 and 4.4.4 and complete proof, printed pp. 235–237.

source_review.read_extent: Read all of Section 4.4, including the first-passage inequality, the layer-cake proof of Theorem 4.4.4, and its monotone-limit step, printed pp. 235–237.
source_review.supports: An independent book treatment of the discrete martingale inequality used on finite time grids.
source_review.limitations: It is a discrete-time inequality; the local proof supplies the continuous-time dyadic limit.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete transition-kernel definition and Markov property discussion in Section 5.2.
source_review.supports: A comparison for the conditional transition convention.
source_review.limitations: The local item defines its continuous-time finite-rate chain and proves the semigroup martingale directly.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete Section 4.4 finite-state continuous-time Markov-chain theorems and proofs, printed pp. 235–237, and Section 5.2 for the kernel convention.
source_review.supports: The finite-state generator and transition-matrix convention used in the local construction.
source_review.limitations: The published result is used for comparison only; the local proof handles all reducible and absorbing cases.

source_review.read_extent: Read Section 4.4, Theorems 4.4.2 and 4.4.4 with their complete proofs, and Section 5.2, printed pp. 235–237 and 273–275.
source_review.supports: The finite-state continuous-time generator and transition convention.
source_review.limitations: The local definition fixes row action and uniformization; no irreducibility or reversibility is required.

sources.title: David Aldous and James Allen Fill, Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, complete author-hosted book

contents.name: Finite continuous-time rate matrices and jump-and-hold construction

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete Section 2.1.2, including its rate-matrix convention, generator, jump chain, exponential holding times, and transition semigroup, printed pp. 25–27.
source_review.supports: The finite-state rate-matrix and transition-semigroup conventions.
source_review.limitations: The book's chapter assumes an irreducible chain and its jump-and-hold formula requires positive exit rates; the local uniformization proof covers reducible generators and absorbing states.

source_review.read_extent: Read the same complete continuous-time construction and its stated irreducibility scope.
source_review.supports: A comparison treatment for exponential clock constructions and the matrix semigroup.
source_review.limitations: The local proof uses a constant-rate uniformization that proves the broader finite-generator statement.

sources.title: Hugo Touchette, The large deviation approach to statistical mechanics
sources.locator: Section II, empirical vector equations (15)–(18), PDF pp. 8–10.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete empirical-vector example from its multinomial law through equation (18) and the rate-function interpretation.
source_review.supports: The finite relative-entropy expression for empirical probability vectors.
source_review.limitations: This is a large-deviation rate-function discussion, not a proof of the chain rule or data-processing inequality; those are proved locally.

sources.title: Olav Kallenberg, Foundations of Modern Probability, 1997
sources.locator: Chapter 4, Theorem 4.19 and Lemma 4.20, printed pp. 75–77.

contents.name: Vague topology on locally finite measures

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete definition preceding Theorem 4.19 and the full proofs of Theorem 4.19 and Lemma 4.20, printed pp. 75–77.
source_review.supports: The locally finite measure space, vague convergence against compactly supported continuous tests, and the distinction from weak convergence when mass can escape.
source_review.limitations: The item defines local-count uniform integrability as an explicit condition; it asserts no expectation-convergence result from that condition alone.

sources.title: Günter Last and Mathew Penrose, Lectures on the Poisson Process, complete author-hosted book

contents.name: Point processes as counting measures and local finiteness

source_review.read_extent: Read the point-process random-counting-measure definition in Section 2.1 and the complete locally-finite point-process definitions and surrounding metric-space discussion in Section 2.4, printed pp. 9–18.
source_review.supports: The counting-measure configuration and local finiteness convention used in the example.
source_review.limitations: The two contrasting limits and the Bernoulli mark law are constructed and verified locally.

contents.name: Locally finite counting measures and vague tests

source_review.read_extent: Read the point-process definition in Section 2.1 and the complete locally-finite point-process definitions and discussion in Section 2.4, printed pp. 9–18.
source_review.supports: The counting-measure representation, local finiteness, and use of spatial point-measure tests.
source_review.limitations: The local item states its own vague-topology and count-uniform-integrability conventions without deriving expectation convergence from vague convergence.
